analysis.investment_thesis: Aegis Logistics is a well-run LPG and chemical terminal business with a remarkable 22.6% EBITDA CAGR over 9 years, benefiting from India's structural LPG infrastructure buildout. The concern is that total debt has ballooned 5.5x in three years to INR 4,606 Cr, Debt/EBITDA now sits at 3.5x — above my 3x comfort threshold — and EV/EBITDA of 23x prices in continued execution without any buffer for the leverage cycle to turn.
key_strengths: OCF positive in all 5 of the last 5 years with EBITDA compounding at 22.6% CAGR from INR 208 Cr (FY16) to INR 1,298 Cr (FY25) — a decade of consistent delivery
Infrastructure-like terminal assets in strategically located ports create durable competitive moats through high replacement cost and long-term customer contracts
Strong promoter holding of 58.1% provides alignment; net profit compounding at 22.6% CAGR over 9 years reflects operational discipline
key_risks: Debt explosion: total debt grew from INR 835 Cr (FY22) to INR 4,606 Cr (FY25) — a 5.5x increase in three years — Debt/EBITDA at 3.5x exceeds my 3x threshold
Finance costs growing at 28% CAGR, reaching INR 165 Cr in FY25; further rate increases or delays in new terminal ramp-up would squeeze coverage rapidly
FCF was -INR 386 Cr in FY25 after INR 945 Cr capex; revenue has declined from INR 8,627 Cr (FY23) to INR 6,764 Cr (FY25), even if EBITDA margins expanded
red_flags: Debt/EBITDA of 3.5x — if EBITDA growth disappoints or interest rates rise, the leverage amplifies downside dramatically
Other income of INR 208 Cr in FY25 represents ~26% of net profit; quality of earnings inflated by non-operating items
Free cash flow negative in FY2025 despite strong reported profits — capex cycle must deliver or returns disappoint
analysis.detailed_analysis: Aegis has earned genuine respect: compounding EBITDA from INR 208 Cr to INR 1,298 Cr over nine years while maintaining positive OCF is a strong record. The terminal infrastructure business is capital-intensive but creates real competitive barriers through location and scale. Net profit of INR 787 Cr at a P/E of 32x is not outrageously expensive for this quality. But the debt story demands scrutiny — borrowings have gone from INR 253 Cr (FY20) to INR 2,439 Cr (FY25), and total debt per the balance sheet is INR 4,606 Cr. This aggressive expansion is a bet on continued volume growth and regulatory stability in LPG distribution.
